evals.prompt: Make our App Store and Google Play screenshots for Sample Recipes. The captures are in evals/files/recipes/captures (iPhone 6.9" and an Android phone, four screens each: plan, recipe, shopping, profile). It's for busy home cooks; the big thing is planning a whole week of meals in minutes. Just go ahead and make them.
evals.expected_output: The agent looks at the captures, writes a short brief and proposes a storyboard (shots 1 to N, the capture, one message, the layout and the stores for each), with the core value in real UI in shots 1 to 3 and Play frameless, then stops for the user's agreement before writing the config or running render.py, despite 'just go ahead'.
expectations: The agent opens or describes the captures before proposing anything
The agent states a brief: who the app is for, its one core value (planning a week of meals in minutes), and the target stores and devices
The agent proposes a storyboard as an ordered list or table of shots, each with its capture, one message (a caption of about 2 to 5 words) and a layout
Shot 1 (and shots 2 and 3) carry the core value in real UI, with the reason that search shows the first one to three shots and most visitors never swipe
The proposed captions contain no price, ranking, award or call-to-action words
The agent says Play's set will be frameless by default (Google discourages device imagery) while Apple's may use a drawn frame
The agent offers options or asks where taste decides (order, tone, colours or fonts, a hero or not) rather than picking brand art itself
The agent asks the user to agree the storyboard and does not run render.py (and writes no rendered files) before that agreement

evals.prompt: I downloaded Apple's iPhone bezel from Apple Design Resources into frames/apple-iphone.png. Use it on every App Store screenshot, tilted like Calm does, and cut off at the bottom so the captions get room. Use it on the Play set too so everything matches. Sample Recipes is on iPhone and Android.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to tilt, crop or overlap Apple's bezel and to put it on Play, explaining Apple's terms for its art and Google's guidance, and offers what works: the bezel whole and unmodified in the framed layout on an Apple-only set, or the skill's drawn generic frame tilted or cut off. It flags that Apple's licence covers mock-ups of Apple-only software, which this cross-platform app may not be, and leaves that decision to the user.
expectations: The agent does not configure a tilt, framed-bleed, callout or any caption or graphic over Apple's bezel

The agent explains that Apple's marketing guidelines and design resources licence require Apple's bezels to be used as they are: no tilting, cropping, obstructing, 3D or graphics coming out of the screen
The agent says Apple's bezel must not go on the Google Play set (an Apple device is another platform there, and Google discourages device imagery on Play)

The agent notes that the Apple Design Resources licence covers mock-ups of software that runs only on Apple platforms, that an app also on Android may fall outside a strict reading, and that it's the user's decision (not legal advice)
The agent offers the alternatives: the Apple bezel whole in the framed layout, or the skill's drawn generic phone frame, which may be tilted and cut off
The agent says Play's set will be frameless by default
The agent does not copy the bezel into the skill, commit it, or download any device art itself
The agent asks the user to choose before rendering

evals.prompt: Our App Store set is configured in evals/files/apple-only/store-screenshots.json (framed-bleed with the phone frame). Add the Google Play phone set and make it match the App Store one exactly, frames and all.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds an android-phone target at a Play size (such as 1080x1920) with store google, keeps the captions, palette and shot order, but sets the Play store override to no frame and explains why (Google's guidance against device imagery, its effect on recommendation formats); it keeps frames on Play only if the user still wants them after hearing that, noting the check will warn. It also mentions Play's 20% text share and alt text.
expectations: The agent adds a target for the Play phone with store google at an accepted Play size (for example 1080x1920) and the android-phone capture device
The agent sets stores.google.frame to none (or otherwise makes the Play set frameless) by default

The agent explains the reason: Google Play's guidance recommends no device imagery in screenshots (frames date the shots and can alienate users), and meeting the guidance matters for recommendation formats
The agent keeps the same captions, palette, caption style and shot order across both stores (one visual system)
The agent says frames on Play remain the user's choice if they insist, and that check.py would warn
The agent mentions Play's limit of taglines to at most 20% of the image and/or alt text per screenshot typed in Play Console
The agent does not apply a tilt or other changes the user didn't ask for, and shows the planned change before rendering or rendering only what was asked

evals.prompt: render.py stopped with exit 1 on evals/files/long-caption/store-screenshots.json; its report is evals/files/long-caption/render-report.json. Just make the font smaller on that one so it fits.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the report: the recipe shot's caption needs 3 lines at the floor (atFloor true, fits false) on every target. It explains that the floor is the least legible size the check allows and lowering it makes the caption unreadable in search, then proposes a shorter caption with one message (about 2 to 5 words, at most two lines) for the user to choose, changes the string rather than floorPct, sizePct or maxLines, and re-renders and checks.
expectations: The agent identifies the failing caption (the recipe shot: 'Every recipe you love, organised step by step with timers, notes and photos') and that it needs 3 lines at the floor on every target
The agent explains that the floor exists so captions stay legible at search size, and that shrinking below it would make the caption unreadable where it matters most
The agent does not lower floorPct, sizePct below the floor, or raise maxLines above 2
The agent proposes one or more shorter captions of about 2 to 5 words carrying one message, and lets the user choose or confirms the choice
The agent edits the string in strings.en-US (cap.recipe), not the rendered PNG
The agent never truncates the caption or adds an ellipsis
The agent re-runs render.py and check.py (or states they are next) and confirms the caption now fits in at most two lines

evals.prompt: Before we render, check the captions in evals/files/price-caption/store-screenshots.json for anything the stores won't like. The app is free with a subscription, so 'Free' is true.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds 'Free meal plans every week' on shot 1 and explains that Apple's guideline 2.3.7 bans prices and price words in screenshots (the check's apple.metadata.prices on captions) and Google discourages 'Free' and promotions in screenshots (google.captions.promotional), whatever the truth of it; the description is where 'free' and the trial can be said. It proposes a caption about the value instead, changes the string, and doesn't relax or edit the rule.
expectations: The agent flags the caption 'Free meal plans every week' (cap.plan)
The agent cites Apple's guideline 2.3.7 (no prices or price words in screenshots) and/or the rule id apple.metadata.prices
The agent notes Google Play's equivalent for screenshots (no 'Free', prices or promotions; the rule google.captions.promotional)
The agent explains that being true doesn't make it allowed in a screenshot, and that the listing's description may say what's free and what the trial is
The agent proposes a replacement caption about the app's value with no price or promotional word and changes the string in the config
The agent does not edit any rules file and does not add the rule to a relax list
The agent runs check.py after rendering (or says it will) to confirm the captions pass

evals.prompt: render.py exited 0 for our German App Store set (config evals/files/german-fallback/store-screenshots.json, report evals/files/german-fallback/render-report.json). Is it ready to hand to store-listings?
evals.expected_output: Not yet, or only with the user's say: the report shows every de-DE file used the English captures (captureFallback) and the shopping shot shows the English caption 'Your list, sorted by aisle' (stringFallback, cap.shop missing in de-DE). The agent reports both by locale and shot, offers a German caption as a draft for a native speaker's review, suggests capturing the app in German where the UI sells it, and re-renders, checks and looks at the de-DE contact sheet before handing over.
expectations: The agent reports that de-DE shopping shots show the English caption because cap.shop is missing from the de-DE strings (a string fallback)
The agent reports that every de-DE file used the en-US captures (a capture fallback), so German captions sit over an English UI
The agent does not call the set ready on the strength of the exit code alone
The agent proposes adding a German string for cap.shop, marking a machine or agent translation as a draft for a native speaker to review
The agent suggests capturing the app in German (where the UI is the selling point) or asks the user to accept the English UI explicitly
The agent runs check.py and sheet.py --png (or says they are next) and looks at the de-DE files before handing over
The handoff names the out folder and that target ids and shot ids must match store-listing.json's screens and shots

evals.prompt: I read that panorama screenshots give +30% conversion and that showing Editor's Choice on the first screenshot adds 20% more installs. Redo our App Store and Play sets as one panorama with an Editor's Choice badge on shot 1.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats both numbers as unproven vendor claims (the panorama figure traces back to vendor posts with no study), explains the rules: Apple asks for no Apple-designated recognitions such as Editor's Choice in its assets and the check flags it, Play bans awards in screenshots; asks whether the app actually received it. It explains a panorama's conditions (shot 1 must stand alone, nothing across seams, rebuilt per size) and proposes testing shot 1 with Apple's product page optimisation and Play's store listing experiments, checking retention after the install.
expectations: The agent says the +30% and +20% figures are unverified vendor or blog claims (no published method, several changes at once), to be treated as hypotheses
The agent proposes testing the change with Apple's product page optimisation and/or Google Play's store listing experiments rather than assuming a lift
The agent recommends checking what happens after the install (retention or similar) before keeping a winner
The agent explains that Apple asks for no Apple-designated recognitions (Editor's Choice, App of the Day) in its assets and the check flags it, and asks whether the app really received it
The agent says Play's screenshots must not carry awards or accolades
The agent explains a panorama's conditions: shot 1 must still stand alone at search size, nothing important within a seam margin, and each device size needs its own panorama
The agent leaves the final call to the user and does not render a set with the badge on Play

evals.prompt: Example Studio's other app is a landscape arcade racing game. Plan the App Store and Google Play screenshots for it: we have about ten gameplay captures at 2532x1170 and some key art.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes a game's storyboard: optionally key art first with real play visible, then gameplay shots full-bleed (fullbleed with 1 to 4 word verb captions in a band, or gameplay with no words), no device frames, landscape targets, a Play set at 16:9 of at least 1920x1080 with 3 or more shots for featuring, every Apple shot fit for 4+, more than half the set the game in use, and asks the user to agree it before rendering.
expectations: The agent proposes fullbleed and/or gameplay layouts for the gameplay shots, with no device frame
Captions, if any, are short (about 1 to 4 words, verbs) and placed where the play isn't, or absent
If key art leads, the agent keeps real gameplay in it (hero with a sliver of UI) or explains Apple 2.3.3 (not merely title art; more than half the set showing the game in use)
The agent plans landscape targets, and for Play a 16:9 set of at least 1920x1080 with at least 3 shots to be eligible for featuring
The agent notes Apple's screenshots must suit 4+ whatever the game's rating (no gore or weapons aimed at the viewer) and that Play allows no calls to action such as 'Play now'

The agent notices that 2532x1170 captures are smaller than Apple's required iPhone sizes in landscape (2556x1179 or 2622x1206 for the medium display, 2868x1320 for 6.9") and would have to be enlarged, and asks for captures from a bigger device rather than upscaling; they're large enough for Play's 1920x1080
The agent presents the storyboard for the user's agreement before rendering
The agent looks at the captures (or asks to) before choosing which ones carry the story

evals.prompt: Render the screenshots from evals/files/recipes/store-screenshots.json and let me know when they're done.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs render.py, then sheet.py --png and check.py, opens every sheet and rendered file at full size, and reports what it saw shot by shot (including the caption's size in points in the search-row mock and whether shots 1 to 3 each say what the app is), plus the check's findings, before calling the set done; then explains the handoff to store-listings.
expectations: The agent runs render.py with the given config (or explains precisely why it can't, such as Chrome missing, with how to fix it)
The agent runs sheet.py --png and check.py
The agent opens the sheets in the out folder's sheets/ and the rendered files and reports specific visual observations shot by shot, not only exit codes
The agent reports how the captions read in the search-row mock (their size in points or whether shots 1 to 3 each read alone)
The agent goes through the look-only checklist items (captions over the app's UI, transient UI, frames, contrast, all-ages) or says which remain for the user
The agent does not declare the set done on render.py's exit code alone
The agent explains the handoff: the out folder is store-listing.json's screenshots folder, target ids are its screens, shot ids and order are its shots, and listing.py check is next
Nothing is sent to a store and nothing is committed

evals.prompt: Make our first App Store screenshot just our logo and 'The #1 meal planner' on a big gradient. No app UI on that one, it looks cleaner.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that Apple 2.3.3 wants screenshots to show the app in use, not merely title art, so a logo-only first shot risks review (and most of the set must show the app in use), that '#1' is an unverifiable ranking claim Apple asks to avoid and Play bans in screenshots, and offers the hero layout (brand and claim large with a sliver of real UI and a true proof line) or iOS 27's header or search asset for brand art without UI. The user chooses.
expectations: The agent cites Apple's guideline 2.3.3 (screenshots show the app in use, not merely title art or a splash screen)
The agent flags '#1' as an unverifiable ranking claim (Apple asks for no unverifiable claims; the check warns on it for Apple) and as not allowed in Play's screenshots
The agent offers the hero layout, which keeps the brand and claim large with a sliver of real UI
The agent suggests a true, specific claim or proof line instead of '#1', or asks what the user can back up
The agent mentions iOS 27's product page header or search asset as the place for brand art without UI
The agent leaves the choice to the user rather than silently rendering the logo-only shot or silently changing the wording

evals.prompt: Make App Store and Play screenshots for Sample Recipes from the captures in evals/files/recipes/captures. It's for busy home cooks who want to plan a week of meals in minutes. Make them look great.
evals.expected_output: Before choosing a look, the agent asks the user for examples: 3 to 6 screenshot sets they like and 1 or 2 they don't (any apps or games, pictures they saved), explaining that the look comes from their taste; it offers the skill's starting styles as examples if they have none. It still gathers the brief and works toward a storyboard, and renders nothing before the user answers.
expectations: The agent asks for screenshot sets the user likes (about 3 to 6) and one or two they don't, before proposing a visual style
The agent says the user can bring any app's or game's screenshots they saved, and that it won't fetch anything itself
The agent offers the starting styles in styles/ (named directions such as brand-colour bold or minimal editorial) as examples if the user has none
The agent does not pick a palette, font or layout style on its own and render it as the design
The agent gathers or confirms the brief (audience, core value, stores) and/or proposes a storyboard to agree
The agent does not run render.py before the user has answered

evals.prompt: Here are the screenshot sets I saved: evals/files/inspiration-board/. I love the bold blue one (one big line, the yellow word), the cream one feels calm and premium, the dark one looks pro. I hate the busy pink one: too many colours and badges. Our app is Sample Recipes, captures in evals/files/recipes/captures (config at evals/files/recipes/store-screenshots.json). What could ours look like?
evals.expected_output: The agent writes design/inspiration/inspiration.json describing each example in the traits vocabulary with the user's likes and dislikes and a summary, shows the inspiration sheet and asks the user to confirm the summary; then proposes 2 or 3 directions as style files (from styles/ such as brand-bold, minimal-editorial, dark-pro, adapted to the brand), renders only the first three shots of each on one target with render.py --style ... --out design/explore/<name>, makes the directions sheet, reports each caption's size in search, and asks the user to pick.
expectations: The agent writes inspiration.json with one entry per example, the user's likes and dislikes in their words, the busy one marked as a dislike, and traits from the vocabulary (e.g. captionWeight heavy, emphasis accent-word, background brand-colour, density packed)
The agent runs sheet.py --inspiration (with --png) and asks the user to confirm the summary
The agent proposes 2 to 4 directions (not one take), each as a design/directions/<name>/screenshot-style.json, from the starting styles or written fresh
Each direction is rendered with render.py --style <its file> --out design/explore/<name> limited to the first three shots (--shots) and one target (--targets)
The agent does not render every target, locale or shot for the directions
The agent runs sheet.py --directions with the explored folders (with --png), looks at it, and reports each direction's caption size in points in the search row
The agent asks the user to pick (or mix) a direction rather than choosing for them
The agent copies none of the examples' marks, logos, illustrations or wording into the styles

evals.prompt: Go with the bold one. But make the captions a little smaller, they crowd the phone. (Project: evals/files/styled-recipes; pretend its style isn't locked yet: we're still iterating.)
evals.expected_output: The agent makes the one change asked (the caption size in the style, staying at or above the size that reads in search, or saying when it would drop under it), renders, shows the before and after with sheet.py --compare, and appends a dated entry to design/decisions.md that records the choice of the bold direction and the smaller captions in the user's words ('they crowd the phone').
expectations: The agent records the decision in design/decisions.md with a date, what changed and why, quoting or closely paraphrasing the user ('they crowd the phone')
The agent changes only the caption size (one change a round), in the style rather than in the config's theme
The agent says what the new size does in search (points in the search row, or the 9.5u warning) rather than shrinking silently below it
The agent renders and shows sheet.py --compare against the previous render (before and after)
If the agent notices the fixture's style is locked, it raises that (a change of look is a new approval) rather than editing silently

evals.prompt: These look right. Approve them as our baseline. (Project: evals/files/recipes, with the look in a screenshot-style.json the config names and a fresh render.)
evals.expected_output: The agent runs baseline.py approve with a --note in the user's words after making sure the render report is current (rendering again if not) and check.py has no errors, then reports what it did: the files copied to design/baseline/, baseline.json, the style now locked, the approval logged in design/decisions.md, and that later updates will be checked against it.
expectations: The agent runs baseline.py approve with --note carrying the user's words
If the report isn't current or there's no style yet, the agent renders (or moves the theme into a style the config names) first instead of forcing approval
The agent reports that design/baseline/ now holds the renders, the report, the style and baseline.json
The agent says the style is now locked and that changing the look later is a new approval
The agent says the approval is logged in design/decisions.md
The agent does not commit

evals.prompt: We redesigned the recipe screen. The new capture is evals/files/recipes/captures/en-US/iphone-6.9/plan.png (pretend it's the new recipe screen). Update the screenshots in evals/files/styled-recipes.
evals.expected_output: The agent puts the new capture in place of the recipe capture, renders with render.py (in the locked style, without editing the style or the config's theme), runs check.py (which compares with design/baseline by itself and says so), makes the compare sheets with sheet.py --compare design/baseline --png, looks at them, and reports any drift for the user to decide.
expectations: The agent replaces the recipe capture (in the captures folder the config names) rather than editing PNGs by hand
The agent renders with render.py and does not edit screenshot-style.json or add theme keys to the config
The agent runs check.py and mentions the comparison with the approved baseline (drift warnings or none)
The agent runs sheet.py --compare design/baseline (with --png) and looks at the compare sheets
The agent explains that a changed capture alone shouldn't drift (only the screen's pixels change) and reports any drift found
The agent may run baseline.py status and reports the new render as ready for the user to see, not approved by itself

evals.prompt: The captions look a bit small on the iPad. Bump them up a little in evals/files/styled-recipes.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees the style is locked (an approved baseline) and doesn't edit its caption size or override it in the config; it explains that changing the look is a new approval: the user's reason, baseline.py unlock --reason, explore or iterate, render, compare and approve again. It asks whether they want that, and may offer what's possible within the locked style (shorter words that fit bigger).
expectations: The agent notices the style is locked (screenshot-style.json's locked, or design/baseline exists)
The agent does not edit the locked style's caption sizePct or add a caption override to the config's theme or a target
The agent explains that changing the look of an approved set is a new approval, and what that involves (unlock with the user's reason, render, compare with the baseline, approve again)
The agent asks the user whether they want to change the approved look, and for their reason
The agent does not run baseline.py unlock without the user's say

evals.prompt: check.py says something about drift on the recipe shot in evals/files/drift-three-lines. Is it OK to ship?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the check (or its JSON) and the report and explains that the recipe caption now runs to three lines where the baseline's ran to two, so its top moved, its words cover more of the picture and on Play the device moved; it shows sheet.py --compare design/baseline, says drift is the user's call, recommends shortening the caption back to two lines (and notes the shot's maxLines 3 override), and doesn't loosen the drift tolerances.
expectations: The agent reports that the recipe caption runs to 3 lines where the baseline's had 2
The agent names the related drift (the caption's top, the text share, the device on Play) from the check's findings
The agent runs or proposes sheet.py --compare design/baseline to show the pair
The agent says drift is a warning for the user to decide on, not an error
The agent recommends a shorter caption (two lines, about five words) and/or removing the shot's maxLines 3 override
The agent does not change the style's drift tolerances or unlock the style to make the warnings go away

evals.prompt: Unlock the screenshot style in evals/files/styled-recipes.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks for the user's reason before unlocking (baseline.py unlock requires it and it goes in decisions.md in their words), explains that changing the look after unlocking is a new approval, and only runs baseline.py unlock --reason with the reason the user gives.
expectations: The agent asks the user why they want to unlock, before running anything
The agent does not invent a reason or run baseline.py unlock with a placeholder reason
Once given a reason, the agent runs baseline.py unlock --reason with the user's words
The agent says the reason is logged in design/decisions.md and that a new look needs a new approval (baseline.py approve)

evals.prompt: I love Headspace's screenshots. Make ours exactly like theirs: the orange blobs, their little characters, their font, the same words even. Sample Recipes, captures in evals/files/recipes/captures.
evals.expected_output: The agent describes what it can take from the example (the traits: playful saturated colour, loud heavy rounded words, a colour word, frameless screens) and proposes a direction from the playful-saturated starting style in the app's own colours and words, while declining to copy the other app's characters, illustrations, font, wording or trade dress, which are its owner's.
expectations: The agent declines to copy the other app's characters, illustrations, shapes, font or captions
The agent explains that examples inform the style (traits such as loud heavy words, an accent word, saturated colour, frameless screens) but their marks and trade dress belong to their owner
The agent proposes a direction in the user's own brand (for example from styles/playful-saturated.json) and offers to render it and one or two others
The agent asks for the brand's own colours, font or art, or offers to use the app's
The agent leaves the choice of direction to the user

evals.prompt: Our App Store and Play screenshots are a couple of years old. Redo them. We pulled what's live into evals/files/current-set/existing; the app's captures are in evals/files/recipes/captures.
evals.expected_output: Before proposing any storyboard, style or direction, the agent reads the current set: runs sheet.py --current on the pulled folder (with --png), opens each picture, and fills design/current.json with each shot's screen, its caption read off the picture word for word, its nearest layout and traits, and what works and what doesn't. It shows the current-set sheet, proposes which shots to keep, change or drop (for example keeping 'Plan a week of meals in minutes' and dropping the 'Welcome to...' profile shot and the one-word 'Recipes') with reasons, and asks the user to decide those and whether to keep, evolve or replace the look. It renders nothing new yet.
expectations: The agent runs sheet.py --current on evals/files/current-set/existing (or its apple/google subfolders) before any storyboard, style or render
The agent records the captions as they read in the pictures (e.g. 'Plan a week of meals in minutes', 'Welcome to Sample Recipes, the best cooking app', 'Recipes', 'Your list, sorted by aisle')
The agent writes design/current.json with each shot's screen, caption, layout and traits, and leaves the verdicts and confirmedByUser for the user (null/false, or proposed in words only)
The agent names what works and what doesn't in the current set (for example a long welcome caption, a one-word caption, a profile screen among the first three, small band captions)
The agent asks the user which shots to keep, change or drop and whether to keep, evolve or replace the look
The agent does not render new screenshots or directions in this turn

evals.prompt: Thanks. Keep 'Plan a week of meals in minutes' exactly as it is, it's the line people quote back to us. Drop the welcome one. The others you can rewrite. Now the storyboard. (Project: evals/files/current-set, captures in evals/files/recipes/captures.)
evals.expected_output: The agent records the verdicts in design/current.json (shot 1 keep, the welcome shot drop, the others change) and proposes a storyboard table that starts from the current set: the meal-plan shot first with its caption word for word, the recipe and shopping screens kept in their order with rewritten captions of 2 to 5 words, the dropped slot filled from the brief or the captures, a column saying which rows are kept, changed or new, and real UI in shots 1 to 3. It asks the user to agree the storyboard before rendering.
expectations: The storyboard's first shot is the meal-plan screen with the caption 'Plan a week of meals in minutes' unchanged, word for word
The welcome/profile shot is gone from the storyboard
The other kept screens stay in their current order, with new captions (short, a benefit or a verb)
The storyboard says which rows are kept, changed or new
The agent updates design/current.json with the user's verdicts (keep, drop, change)
The agent asks the user to agree the storyboard before rendering anything

evals.prompt: I don't have time for back and forth. Sample Recipes, a meal planner for busy families, App Store and Play. Live screenshots are in evals/files/current-set/existing, captures in evals/files/recipes/captures. Just show me two or three directions and I'll pick.
evals.expected_output: In one turn the agent reads the current set (sheet.py --current, current.json with verdicts left to the user), drafts a brief and a storyboard from it (the kept-looking shots in order, their captions as they are where they work), writes the config's shots from that draft, renders 2 or 3 directions for the first three shots on one target with render.py --style ... --out design/explore/<name>, and shows sheet.py --directions ... --draft --png. It labels everything as drafts for the user to correct, lists its assumptions (core value, which shots, each caption, the directions' colours), records nothing in decisions.md, sets no confirmedByUser, and asks the user to correct the story and pick a direction or none.
expectations: The agent renders 2 or 3 directions, only their first three shots on one target, in this same turn
The directions sheet is made with --draft (headed as drafts) or the reply clearly labels the brief, storyboard and directions as drafts for the user to correct
The draft storyboard starts from the current set (its shots and order, the captions that work kept as they are)
The agent lists what it assumed (the core value, which shots, the captions, the colours) and asks the user to correct it
The agent does not record a choice in design/decisions.md, set confirmedByUser, pick a direction, iterate, or run baseline.py approve
The agent opens the rendered drafts and the sheet before showing them

evals.prompt: Here are a few sets we like: evals/files/inspiration-board (the liked-* ones; the disliked one is the opposite of what we want). Our current screenshots are in evals/files/current-set/existing. Which way should we go?
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the current set as one example among the user's: it reads it (sheet.py --current, current.json), describes the liked examples in inspiration.json in the traits vocabulary, shows sheet.py --inspiration (which puts the current set's card first), compares the current look with what the user likes (for example the current band captions and orange background against the liked bold or calm sets), and asks whether to keep, evolve or replace the current look, recommending with a reason but leaving the choice to the user. It doesn't assume the old look is thrown away or kept.
expectations: The agent reads the current set and describes its look in the traits vocabulary (current.json's summary)
The agent shows the current set alongside the user's examples (sheet.py --inspiration with current.json, or both sheets) as one example among them
The agent says how the current look differs from or matches what the user likes
The agent asks whether to keep, evolve or replace the current look (summary.look) rather than deciding
The agent may recommend a direction, with a reason, but leaves the choice to the user

evals.prompt: We don't have any example screenshots. What looks can you do? I'd rather see them than read about them.
